interventions.speaker: EXPERT-COHORT
interventions.who: cohort criterion; what the labelled series did in this exact situation
interventions.body:
This patient's situation: prior positive biopsy. The panel alone does not answer, and that is the finding.

The criterion here is that the visible panel does not determine this decision: he already has a tissue diagnosis, so neither a high PI-RADS nor a rising PSA is new information. What decides it is the documented grade of the prior biopsy and the surveillance history, which live in the previous notes. Measured on the labelled series: none of the three panel
rules I carry for this situation (PSA >= 20, age >= 78, PI-RADS <= 2) applies to him, and among the
39 remaining labelled men in this situation no structured variable separates the two answers.

REGISTRAR: the previous notes are where this case is decided. Read them for the grade of the prior
biopsy (Gleason or ISUP), the number of biopsy sessions and their dates, and whether he is on a
surveillance protocol with a confirmatory biopsy due. Do not read this as 'defer' and do not read it
as 'biopsy'.

interventions.body:
The case library holds 48 labelled men in this same situation (Positive prior biopsy). The 3 closest by panel distance, and what the reading urologist did:
  1. distance 0.35: PI-RADS 5, PSA 8.6, PSAD 0.202, age 68, DRE Nodus -> BIOPSY (clear). He wrote: "Patient reasonable to discuss curative treatment with (age 68, no very dramatic comorbidity, unfavorable intermediate risk disease). Considering he chose not curative tr…"
  2. distance 0.36: PI-RADS 5, PSA 8.3, PSAD 0.215, age 66, DRE Suspicious -> DEFER (clear). He wrote: "This person should discuss curative treatment (younger patient with palpable, MRI-visible high-risk disease incl Gleason 5 findings). If not curative treatment for any r…"
  3. distance 0.60: PI-RADS 5, PSA 6.9, PSAD 0.257, age 67, DRE Nodus -> BIOPSY (uncertain). He wrote: "What was the result of the earlier positive biopsy and the MRI precluding that biopsy? Hard to determine what we are looking at here."

PRECEDENT: BIOPSY (weighted vote 0.63 for biopsy). Distance-weighted precedent is no better than chance here (0.47 leave-one-out): read the precedents for how this urologist reasons, not for the answer.

What the precedents are FOR: they show what this urologist looks at and how he phrases the call. What they are NOT: facts about this patient. Nobody may cite a precedent's grade, PSA or MRI as if it were his.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The EAU guidelines suggest that a PI-RADS score of 5 mandates a repeat biopsy to confirm histological progression before a change in treatment strategy. The guideline also states that targeted and perilesional biopsy cores should be taken if a confirmatory or repeat biopsy is performed.

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
EXPERT-STRUCTURED's suggestion of no biopsy is not decisive because the guideline mandates a repeat biopsy when a PI-RADS score of 5 is present. EXPERT-LIBRARY's precedent suggests a biopsy in one case, while EXPERT-TRACE suggests weighing the prior biopsy and DRE, which are key variables the guideline does not override.

WHAT WE STILL NEED
The prior biopsy status is known as 'Positive', which is a fact that the guideline makes it decide.
The PI-RADS score is known as '5', which is a fact that the guideline makes it decide.
The DRE finding is known as 'Nodus', which is a fact that the guideline makes it decide.
The prior biopsy status is known as 'Positive', which is a fact that the guideline makes it decide.
The PSA is known as '6.9 ng/mL', which is a fact that the guideline makes it decide.

REGISTRAR — pull these up, and answer exactly the question attached to each:

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: INDETERMINATE (uncertain). Last value 6.90 ng/mL over 3 points spanning 28 months; velocity +2.66 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 8 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 8.3 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 2.4-28.8.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.body:
Expert 3 here — the fusion classifier. I read the panel, the mpMRI report and the laboratory panel; nothing from the previous notes or the PSA series.

SUGGESTION: NO BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.40
  uncertainty  +/- 0.16 epistemic (95% band 0.08-0.72), of which 0.00 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  LOW ('discuss' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 61% of the time over the 31 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. Out-of-fold AUC 0.794. I am the only expert that has read the report's wording, and I still cannot see the prior grade or the

interventions.speaker: PANEL-PROTOCOL
interventions.who: the panel's written protocol; consolidates the experts by rule and says which rule fired
interventions.body:
The panel protocol, applied to what is on the board:

  EXPERT-STRUCTURED  DEFER, p(biopsy)=0.44  ('discuss' tier; weight 1.0)
  EXPERT-FUSION      DEFER, p(biopsy)=0.40  ('discuss' tier, fusion_full; weight 1.5)
  EXPERT-LIBRARY     BIOPSY, p(biopsy)=0.63  (k=3 precedents; does not vote)

  documented prior grade in the opened documents: GG 2 ("Gleason 3+4")

RULE THAT FIRED: documented prior grade GG 2 (Gleason 3+4) — carried by documented grade.
PANEL ANSWER: NO BIOPSY. A documented grade group of 2 or more is a treatment problem, not a sampling problem: the reading urologist deferred re-biopsy in 7 of the 8 labelled men with a recorded GG >= 2.
Dissenting on the board: EXPERT-LIBRARY. Their bids are recorded above; they did not carry because a higher rung of the protocol applied.

Confidence the trace model expects here: clear. Weights it expects: bx=important, fh=noted, age=important, dre=important, psa=important, vol=noted, psad=noted, pirads=important, comorbidity=noted.

CHAIR: this is the panel's position. You sign it, and you write why in the room's words — naming what the registrar retrieved. If you believe a retrieved finding overturns it, name that finding with its value; the burden is on the finding, not on the panel.

interventions.speaker: VERIFIER

interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents retrieved by the registrar appear to have answered both open questions. The `previous_notes` provided the prior grade (Gleason 3+4) and the number of biopsy sessions (1), and confirmed an ongoing active surveillance protocol.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The retrieved finding, "PRIOR GRADE: Gleason 3+4 malignancy," aligns with the PANEL-PROTOCOL's answer of NO BIOPSY, as the protocol states that a documented grade group of 2 or more is a treatment problem, not a sampling problem.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. What was the grade (Gleason/ISUP) and number of prior biopsy sessions? Answered by `previous_notes`: Gleason 3+4 malignancy and 1 biopsy session.
Q2. Is the patient currently on a surveillance protocol with a confirmatory biopsy due? Answered by `previous_notes`: Ongoing active surveillance has tracked his biomarker trajectory.

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The documented prior grade (Gleason 3+4) is the most critical variable because the PANEL-PROTOCOL explicitly states this finding is the rule that fired, overriding other expert opinions.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
I suggest the decision should stand as NO BIOPSY, firmly based on the PANEL-PROTOCOL's rule that a documented Gleason 3+4 is a treatment problem, which is what the retrieved documents confirmed.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: defer | MISSING: none
